questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding lithium-induced tremors are true EXCEPT:

options.text: Lithium tremors respond to treatment with metoprolol
Lithium tremors tend to be slow and rhythmic
Lithium tremors are made worse by movement

correct_answer.text: Lithium tremors tend to be slow and rhythmic

correct_answers.text: Lithium tremors tend to be slow and rhythmic

questions.explanation: Lithium tremors tend to be coarse and present at rest.

questions.question_text: Which of the following benzodiazepines has the longest half-life?
questions.explanation: Flurazepam has the longest half-life of 40 to 250 hours.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the primary reason for monitoring plasma Nortriptyline concentrations during the treatment of major depression?

options.text: Clinical correlation of efficacy and adequate dosing
The existence of a curvilinear therapeutic window
To monitor the risk of cardiac toxicity

correct_answer.text: The existence of a curvilinear therapeutic window

correct_answers.text: The existence of a curvilinear therapeutic window

questions.explanation: The primary reason for monitoring plasma Nortriptyline concentrations is for the existence of a curvilinear therapeutic window.

questions.question_text: According to positron emission tomography (PET) studies, what percentage of D2 receptor occupancy correlates with maximal antipsychotic efficacy?
questions.explanation: PET studies indicate that 65% to 70% of D2 receptor occupancy correlates with maximal antipsychotic efficacy.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding the management of overdose with TCAs is true?

options.text: Lidocaine is the first line of treatment
Ammonium chloride is the first line of treatment
Dialysis is the first line of treatment

questions.explanation: Activated charcoal can be administered up to 12 hours after TCA overdose.

questions.question_text: Which of the following accurately describes lithium exposure and neonatal outcome?

options.text: Stopping lithium 1 to 2 days before delivery is likely to improve the neonatal outcomes
Higher neonatal lithium concentrations are associated with higher rates of CNS complications
Higher neonatal lithium levels are associated with significantly lower Apgar scores
Higher neonatal lithium concentrations are associated with higher rates of neuromuscular complications

questions.explanation: Higher neonatal lithium concentrations are associated with significantly lower Apgar scores and higher CNS and neuromuscular complications.

questions.question_text: All of the following are sexual side effects seen in women receiving trazodone EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Sexual side effects in women on trazodone therapy include priapism of the clitoris, spontaneous orgasm, and changes in libido.

questions.question_text: Which of the following antipsychotic medications has the lowest propensity to lower the seizure threshold?
questions.explanation: Molindone has the lowest propensity to lower the seizure threshold.

questions.question_text: What is the estimated mortality rate with NMS?
questions.explanation: The corrected answer appears to be commonly referenced between notable ranges.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true regarding asenapine EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Asenapine is well tolerated and has neutral metabolic effects among listed parameters.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding therapeutic drug monitoring with lithium EXCEPT:

options.text: There is a point of care/office-based test for serum lithium commercially available
Steady state lithium levels are attained after 2 days of constant dosing
Serum lithium levels 12 hours post dose are 30% higher in patients taking the sustained release (SR.) preparation compared with the immediate release (IR) preparation
Therapeutic levels for the treatment of acute mania are in the range of 1.0 to 1.5 mEq per L
It is not uncommon to see fluctuating serum lithium levels in geriatric patients in the absence of any dose changes in lithium

correct_answer.text: Steady state lithium levels are attained after 2 days of constant dosing

correct_answers.text: Steady state lithium levels are attained after 2 days of constant dosing

questions.explanation: Steady-state lithium levels are attained after 5 days of dose adjustment.

questions.question_text: A 28-year-old Caucasian woman with bipolar disorder has been taking lithium 900 mg per day for the past 18 months. All of the following preventative measures are recommended during pregnancy on lithium therapy EXCEPT:

options.text: Fetal echocardiogram is recommended between 16 and 18 weeks of gestation
Caution should be exercised regarding maternal NSAID
NSAID should be avoided in neonates
Withhold lithium therapy for 24 to 48 hours before delivery

questions.explanation: Caution should be exercised regarding maternal NSAID use because of potential drug-drug interactions with lithium.

questions.question_text: Which of the following features is/are associated with PDSS?
questions.explanation: PDSS results from probable accidental intravascular injection of olanzapine long-acting preparation.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true regarding lithium EXCEPT:

options.text: Lithium is not metabolized by the liver
Lithium is excreted unchanged by the kidney
Lithium is a naturally occurring cation
Lithium has mild proserotonergic and adrenergic effects

correct_answer.text: Lithium has mild proserotonergic and adrenergic effects

correct_answers.text: Lithium has mild proserotonergic and adrenergic effects

questions.explanation: Lithium has mild proserotonergic effects but no adrenergic effect.

questions.question_text: Under which of the following conditions would ziprasidone be life-threatening?
questions.explanation: Ziprasidone could be life-threatening in patients with QTc >500 milliseconds or with a history of MI.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding leukopenia associated with carbamazepine therapy?

options.text: It resolves spontaneously despite continued treatment
Incidence of leukopenia associated with carbamazepine therapy is 35%
It is a strong indicator of the development of agranulocytosis

correct_answer.text: It resolves spontaneously despite continued treatment

correct_answers.text: It resolves spontaneously despite continued treatment

questions.explanation: Leukopenia associated with carbamazepine therapy does not predispose patients to infections and resolves spontaneously.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most common side effect with MAOI therapy?
questions.explanation: Orthostatic hypotension is a frequent side effect during MAOI therapy.

questions.question_text: All of the following drugs have been linked to serious exfoliative dermatitis, an adverse dermatologic effect, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Carbamazepine, Lamotrigine, phenobarbital, and VPA are all associated with Stevens-Johnson syndrome.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding the epileptogenic effects of bupropion are true EXCEPT:

options.text: History of closed head injury increases the risk of developing seizure
The drug's active metabolite threohydrobupropion is primarily responsible for the occurrence of seizures
Exceeding 150 mg in any single dose is a risk-factor for seizures
Most seizures with bupropion occur within the first several hours after taking the dose

correct_answer.text: The drug's active metabolite threohydrobupropion is primarily responsible for the occurrence of seizures

correct_answers.text: The drug's active metabolite threohydrobupropion is primarily responsible for the occurrence of seizures

questions.explanation: Threohydrobupropion is less potent than bupropion, hence not responsible for the occurrence of seizures.

questions.question_text: A 38-year-old man with schizophrenia on olanzapine and clonazepam therapy develops blasphemous obsessions and ritualized praying and counting. You diagnose him with comorbid OCD. Assuming you leave his current medications unchanged, which of the following drugs should be avoided in the treatment of his OCD?
questions.explanation: Coadministration of fluvoxamine could result in increased risk of adverse effects from olanzapine.

questions.question_text: All of the following are high-potency benzodiazepine EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Temazepam is a low-potency benzodiazepine; the other listed options are considered high-potency.

questions.question_text: Which of the following over-the-counter medications/food should not be used or used with caution in patients on Selegiline transdermal patch?
questions.explanation: SJW is contraindicated as it may increase the risk of serotonin syndrome and hypertensive crisis.

questions.question_text: Co-administration of lithium and carbamazepine can cause the following additive side effects on all the following organ systems EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Lithium mitigates carbamazepine-induced leukopenia and does not have additive side effects on the hematopoietic system.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the assumed mechanism for antipsychotic-induced QTc prolongation and the risk of torsades de pointes?

options.text: Combined sodium and potassium channel blockade
Blockade of the human ether-a-go-go-related gene (HERG) potassium channel
Blockade of the HERG calcium channel
Combined calcium and potassium channel blockade

correct_answer.text: Blockade of the human ether-a-go-go-related gene (HERG) potassium channel

correct_answers.text: Blockade of the human ether-a-go-go-related gene (HERG) potassium channel

questions.explanation: Antipsychotic-induced QTc prolongation is primarily due to HERG potassium channel blockade.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding the mechanism of action of lithium EXCEPT:

options.text: Lithium alters fos expression through a protein kinase C (PKC) mechanism
Lithium causes a relative depletion of myoinositol in the brain
Lithium alters sodium transport in the nervous system
Lithium significantly inhibits cAMP accumulation through G proteins

questions.explanation: All statements regarding lithium's mechanism of action are true.

questions.question_text: A 32-year-old man with treatment-resistant schizophrenia was admitted to non-smoking psychiatric ICU. After titrating him on clozapine, he was transferred to a step-down unit for another week. Two weeks after his discharge to his home, he relapsed and presented to the ER again. The DDI between clozapine and smoking involves which of the following cytochrome enzymes?
questions.explanation: Smoking induces CYP1A2, which reduces clozapine levels, leading to relapse.

questions.question_text: Management of akathisia includes all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Management options include lowering the neuroleptic dose and initiation of beta-blockers or benzodiazepines.

questions.question_text: A 34-year-old woman with bipolar disorder maintaining well on lithium carbonate comes to you with concerns about worsening acne. The patient reports trying several remedies for her acne; however, none of them have been successful. She appears very frustrated and makes mention of discontinuing lithium. Despite your reassurances, the patient insists on discontinuing lithium and requests you to prescribe an alternative mood stabilizer. You decide to start her on Divalproex sodium. Which of the following concerns should be addressed before the patient leaves your office?

options.text: Potential for a lithium discontinuation syndrome
Potential for reduced efficacy of her acne medication secondary to drug interactions with Divalproex sodium
Potential for her acne medication to induce manic symptoms
Increased risk for depression and suicide from her acne medication

correct_answer.text: Increased risk for depression and suicide from her acne medication

correct_answers.text: Increased risk for depression and suicide from her acne medication

questions.explanation: Isotretinoin for severe cystic acne may worsen affective symptoms, including suicidal ideation in bipolar patients.

questions.question_text: Trazodone's most potent binding property is at which of the following sites?
questions.explanation: Trazodone has potent binding properties at multiple receptor sites including serotonin and histamine receptors.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is/are true regarding advantages of Paliperidone palmitate depot antipsychotic over other available second-generation depot antipsychotics?

options.text: Paliperidone palmitate prefilled syringes require no reconstitution or refrigeration
Paliperidone palmitate does not require an additional precautionary observation period during the post-injection period
Paliperidone palmitate does not require supplementation with oral antipsychotics

questions.explanation: Depot Paliperidone palmitate can be administered monthly and does not have certain restrictions seen with others.

questions.question_text: Drug interactions have known to occur between Divalproex sodium and all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: There are no reported drug-drug interactions between Aripiprazole and Divalproex sodium.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an appropriate loading dose for sodium VPA in the management of acute mania?
questions.explanation: Divalproex sodium 20 mg/kg/day as a loading dose results in rapid resolution of manic symptoms.

questions.question_text: Propranolol should not be combined with all of the following drugs EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: There is no contraindication or DDI between levothyroxine and propranolol.

questions.question_text: MAOI is contraindicated in which of the following medical conditions?
questions.explanation: MAOIs are contraindicated in hepatic disease, renal insufficiency, CHF, and pheochromocytoma.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true regarding the mechanism of VPA's teratogenicity?

options.text: Formation of free radicals during microsomal metabolism of VPA
Inhibition of the enzyme dihydrofolate reductase

correct_answer.text: Formation of free radicals during microsomal metabolism of VPA

correct_answers.text: Formation of free radicals during microsomal metabolism of VPA

questions.explanation: The precise mechanism of VPA's teratogenicity implies formation of free radicals during its metabolism.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements accurately describe the neuromolecular effects of asenapine EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Asenapine has no affinity for muscarinic receptors.

questions.question_text: Which of the following benzodiazepines is used as an adjuvant to lithium in the treatment of mania?
questions.explanation: Clonazepam is commonly used as an adjuvant to lithium in treating mania.

questions.question_text: All of the following conditions can mimic NMS EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: All listed conditions can mimic Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS).

questions.question_text: Which of the following is associated with VPA exposure during pregnancy?
questions.explanation: VPA exposure during pregnancy can lead to hepatotoxicity, coagulopathies, neural tube defects, and hypoglycemia.

questions.question_text: Most adverse effects of carbamazepine are correlated with which of the following plasma concentration?
questions.explanation: Adverse effects of carbamazepine are notably correlated with plasma concentrations greater than 9 μg/ml.

questions.question_text: Genetic polymorphisms in the cytochrome genes can code for inefficient versions of cytochrome enzymes leading to impaired drug metabolism (poor metabolizers). Which of the following ethnic groups carry the highest percentage of poor metabolizers of the CYP2D6 isoenzyme?
questions.explanation: Caucasians exhibit the highest percentage of poor metabolizers of the CYP2D6 isoenzyme.

questions.question_text: The pentobarbital challenge test is used to:

options.text: Determine dosing for treatment refractory tonic-clonic seizures

questions.explanation: The pentobarbital challenge test is utilized to guide detoxification from barbiturates.

questions.question_text: A 49-year-old woman with breast cancer is currently taking tamoxifen. She develops depressive symptoms and is referred to a psychiatrist. She meets the criteria for major depressive disorder. Which of the following medications interacts with tamoxifen?
questions.explanation: Concurrent use of SJW, paroxetine, sertraline, or duloxetine with tamoxifen may result in reduced effectiveness of tamoxifen.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs has shown to cause the most QTc prolongation at therapeutic doses?
questions.explanation: Thioridazine causes the most QTc prolongation at therapeutic doses.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs has none to minimal interactions with the cytochrome isoenzymes?
questions.explanation: Desvenlafaxine has minimal interaction with the CYP system.

questions.question_text: Which of the following properties of Pindolol supports its use as an augmentation agent in the treatment of depression?

options.text: α- Adrenergic and α-adrenergic antagonistic effect

questions.explanation: Pindolol's sympathomimetic effects support its role as an augmentation agent in depression treatment.

questions.question_text: All of the following are antipsychotic-induced adverse effects related to dopamine antagonism EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: All listed effects relate to dopamine antagonism from antipsychotics.

questions.question_text: The CATIE trial, which included 1,493 participants from 57 US institutions, concluded that the greatest body weight gain was observed with which of the following antipsychotics?
questions.explanation: The CATIE trial found the greatest body weight gain associated with olanzapine.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true regarding cardiac side effects during treatment with therapeutic levels of lithium?
questions.explanation: Therapeutic doses of lithium can cause non-specific T wave changes.
